# Cover archival

New archival uses four uncompressed zip files per 10,000 cover IDs (original,
small, medium, large). A cover ID is exactly ten decimal digits, padded with
leading zeroes. The first four digits are the million-cover `item_id`; the next
two digits are the 10,000-cover `batch_id`. For cover `0008810000`, these are
`0008` and `81`.

Each size has a separate archive.org item. The item and local zip paths are:

| Size | Item | Local zip path below `data_root` | Member name |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original | `covers_0008` | `items/covers_0008/covers_0008_81.zip` | `0008810000.jpg` |
| Small | `s_covers_0008` | `items/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_81.zip` | `0008810000-S.jpg` |
| Medium | `m_covers_0008` | `items/m_covers_0008/m_covers_0008_81.zip` | `0008810000-M.jpg` |
| Large | `l_covers_0008` | `items/l_covers_0008/l_covers_0008_81.zip` | `0008810000-L.jpg` |

Remote URLs use `https://archive.org/download/<item>/<zip>/<member>`.

Run `archive.archive()` to stage up to 10,000 unarchived covers. It writes zip
members, closes the zip files, then marks the covers `archived` and sets their
filenames to local zip members. Covers with missing source images are marked
`failed`. To upload and verify a batch, run
`archive.Batch(8, 81).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True)`. Finalization
requires all four zip files to appear in their respective Internet Archive
items. It then sets `uploaded=true`, stores the remote URLs in every filename
field, and removes the local zip files. An unsuccessful upload leaves the staged
zip files and records intact for retry. A shared lock under `items/` prevents
simultaneous local archive and finalization jobs.

Older tar archives and their index files remain readable for legacy covers.

item.text:
Fixed the archival finalization defect. Before updating cover records or deleting local zips, the batch now verifies each remote zip’s MD5 against its local file and requires all four local zips. Archiving also rejects new covers in a batch that already has uploaded records. I updated the web test’s tar assertion for zip output.

The reviewer’s three test commands pass: 5 focused tests, 23 coverstore tests, and 1 webapp test. **TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** seven database integration tests remain skipped because they require PostgreSQL and the `openlibrary` user.
